BiblicalUsage: Garad means to scrape, and it appears once, in Job 2:8, where Job took a potsherd to scrape himself withal, and sat down among the ashes. The word is the sound of a broken man trying to ease his sores with a piece of pottery.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Job's potsherd is one of the saddest pictures in the Bible; he scraped his wounds with broken clay because he had nothing else, and I hold that God saw him there in the ashes and did not look away.
